description: THESAUROS content-storage known-answer tests (design: docs/design-storage.md, spec/platform.md §7). THESAUROS is the platform's O-Foundation content-storage organ over the L4 erasure store. These vectors pin the language-agnostic content-addressing wire so any implementation reproduces content ids (CIDs) and proof-of-retrievability responses byte-for-byte. An object is split into LEAF-sized leaves; each leaf is hashed WITH ITS INDEX (position-bound) and a binary Merkle tree over those leaf hashes gives the CID = the root — the content address and the storage commitment at once. All hashes are BLAKE3 via hash_labeled (BLAKE3 keyed by the 32-byte BLAKE3 hash of the ASCII label). Pinned by the Rust reference suite (fanos-thesauros/tests/conformance.rs). Byte strings are lower-case hex; integers decimal.

params.root: binary Merkle fold of the leaf hashes, duplicating a lone odd node at any level, then WRAPPED with the leaf count: root = hash_labeled(root_label, count_as_u64_be(8) || fold(32)). The count binding is what removes the CVE-2012-2459 ambiguity (unwrapped, [a,b,c] and [a,b,c,c] fold identically) and what fixes the authentication-path length at ceil(log2(count)).
params.cid: the count-bound Merkle root (32 bytes). NOTE: a one-leaf object's CID is NOT its bare leaf hash.
params.path_length: exactly ceil(log2(count)) siblings; any other length must be rejected without hashing
params.path_side: derived from the leaf index parity at each level, never carried in the proof

single_leaf.comment: An object smaller than one leaf is a single leaf; its CID is the count-bound root over that one position-bound leaf hash — deliberately NOT the leaf hash itself, so an id and a leaf hash cannot collide.

two_leaf.comment: 0xAB repeated 4096 (one full leaf) then 0xCD x100 (a partial second leaf). CID = root_label-wrapped node_hash(leaf0, leaf1) with count 2.

leaf1_proof.side_note: leaf 1 is odd, so its sibling is the LEFT child — derived from the index, not carried

por.comment: Proof of retrievability. The audit challenge for a chunk at a beacon is publicly derivable: seed = hash_labeled('FANOS-v1/thesauros-challenge', cid(32) || beacon); successive candidate indices draw(counter) = u64_le(hash_labeled('FANOS-v1/thesauros-draw', seed(32) || counter_u64_le(8)))[0..8] mod leaves, taking the first k DISTINCT (ascending). If k >= leaves the whole chunk is audited. required_samples(lambda, f_tol) = ceil(lambda*ln2 / -ln(1-f_tol)) sets k off-chain. Here: a 16-leaf chunk (leaf i = the byte (i+1) repeated 4096 times), beacon 'epoch-42-beacon', k=5.

manifest.comment: An object of CHUNK*2 + 500 bytes, byte i = (i*7) mod 256, split into 3 chunks (2 full + 1 partial). The manifest encodes count(4, LE) || [ cid(32) || len(4, LE) ] x count; its own CID is chunk_cid(manifest.encode()).
